key_insight: Bringing economic theory into AI governance provides a practical framework to internalize externalities and align incentives so AI systems can be deployed to advance the common good rather than just private returns.
problem_solved: Addresses incentive misalignment and market failures in AI deployment—specifically how private actors can externalize social costs and underprovide public-good outcomes—by offering a tractable economic model and policy levers to correct these failures.
method: Formulate a formal economic model that captures AI-generated externalities, public-good characteristics, and distributional effects on social welfare.

Identify and evaluate policy and incentive instruments (e.g., taxes, subsidies, public investment, governance mechanisms) that internalize externalities and steer private decisions toward common-good outcomes.
Demonstrate the model with illustrative scenarios/simulations or case examples to show how different instruments change incentives and welfare outcomes.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners and policymakers a decision-oriented toolkit to quantify societal costs and benefits, design incentive-compatible deployments, and choose governance interventions that promote equitable, welfare-maximizing AI adoption.
visual_elements: Stakeholder flow diagram showing private firms, users, public sector, and externalities flowing to society
Cost–benefit chart comparing private returns vs. social returns under different policy instruments
Incentive-mechanism schematic (taxes/subsidies/regulation) showing how signals alter firm behavior
Policy toolbox infographic mapping instruments to outcomes (efficiency, equity, innovation)
paper_title: AI economics for the common good
